item.title: Hiker Found Dead on Mount Whitney After Disappearing From Hotel
item.description:
Source: Backpacker Magazine
Mt. Whitney is the highest mountain in the United States outside of Alaska (Photo: Gary Coronado / Contributor via Getty) Search and rescue personnel recovered the body of a missing hiker from California’s Mount Whitney on October 25 following a nearly weeklong effort complicated by early winter storms. In a press release posted to Facebook, the Inyo County Sheriff’s Office (ICSO) said a motel in nearby Lone Pine had notified law enforcement on October 19 that one of its guests had not checked out and had left some of their possessions behind. The office attempted to contact the missing hiker through a law enforcement messaging system, but did not receive a response. While hotel staff knew that the guest had planned to hike, deputies were unsure of their route until the following day, when they discovered the guest’s car parked at Whitney Portal. Upon checking with the U.S. Forest Service, ICSO found that the missing hiker had secured a permit to climb Whitney on October 18. That same day, a helicopter search found a hiker’s body along the Mountaineer’s Route at roughly 13,600 feet. Shortly after that grim discovery, an early-season storm moved into the area, buffeting the Lower 48’s highest peak with strong winds and snow and forcing authorities to postpone the recovery mission. On October 25, after the storm cleared, a California Highway Patrol helicopter was able to carry a SAR team from Inyo County Search and Rescue to Iceberg Lake, a glacial cirque located at about 12,600 feet. From there, rescuers climbed to the hiker’s body and assisted the helicopter in hoisting it off the peak before descending back to the lake for pickup. The Inyo County Coroner’s Office has yet to publicly identify the deceased hiker. The harder of the two most commonly climbed lines up Whitney, the Mountaineer’s Route is 5 miles one way and requires class 3 scrambling in places. The fatality is the second to occur on Whitney this month. In early October, Kalem Peter Kazarian, a contractor who had appeared in a pilot for HGTV, was descending from Whitney’s summit when he fell and suffered fatal injuries. In January, another climber passed away on the “Final 400” section of the Mountaineer’s Route after continuing up the mountain solo while their partner turned back.

item.title: PROFILE: Inside the New D.C. Restaurant That Only Sells Five Curry Steak Frites Every Night
item.description:
Source: Eater
The hottest new spot in Washington, D.C. focuses on the traditional heat-packed cooking methods of northern Thailand, while still using local ingredients from around the DMV. Alfie’s, from chefs Justin Ahn and Alex McCoy, started as a pop-up in Petworth in 2017 before traveling around the world, serving diners in New York and London. This year, the restaurant put down permanent roots in a Georgetown alleyway. The co-owners led us through a day in the new kitchen, preparing everything from hand-cut green papaya in som tam salad to the limited-quantity Thai steak frites with a massaman curry peppercorn sauce. In the video, the kitchen team breaks down rib-eye steaks for their take on a steak au poivre, which they only make five of each night. The steaks are carefully seared for each order, with the au poivre massaman curry sauce is finished in the pan with the leftover beef fat. Classic “bar fries” are served up with the massive 26-ounce rib-eye. Inside the New D.C. Restaurant That Only Sells Five Curry Steak Frites Every Night In a Georgetown alleyway, Alfie’s serves northern Thai dishes that are built around local ingredients Elsewhere in the kitchen, another chef carves green papayas. The irregular slices of papaya get tossed in a funky, spicy dressing for each order. Ko calls it the “most labor intensive dish on the line;” each order is carefully mixed with fresh tomatoes, peanuts, and a palm syrup and tamarind-heavy dressing. A rich pork belly curry is simmering in the background. Gaeng hung lay (a traditional northern Thai curry) cooks down large pieces of pork belly to get that fatty layer, with pickled garlic and pineapple balancing out the rich flavors of curry paste, tamarind, and fish sauce. Right before service, the chefs begin prepping herbs and sticky rice that has been soaking overnight and is quickly steamed for that malleable, glutinous texture. McCoy talks about how being a chef is more of a lifestyle than a job, but there’s immense payoff when you get to see diners enjoy your hard work every night. He hopes that Alfie’s will become a place where “you can just forget where you are, have a good time, and just lose yourself in the experience and the food.” Watch the kitchen team at Aflie’s cook classic Thai dishes and fusion plates like curry steak frites in this episode of Now Open.

item.title: SALES: Planning a European Ski Trip? Let These 11 Airbnbs Guide You to the Right Mountain
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler
Every winter, I find myself looking for an excuse to get back on the mountain. This ski season, I’m looking forward to taking my snow-chasing habit across the Atlantic to the Swiss Alps and staying in one of Europe’s dreamy, idyllic, and ski-ready vacation rentals. While hunting for the perfect Airbnb, I've been fantasizing about future winter trips to the continent: waking to the snow-dusted Dolomites, cozying up in centuries-old lodges in the Alps post-après-ski, or exploring lesser-known Nordic slopes where the northern lights put on a colorful show after dark. Some of the European Airbnbs for ski trips below are so spectacular, they're worth planning an entire winter vacation around. If you’re eyeing the 2026–2027 season (or already plotting next winter’s powder days), start bookmarking now: The best ski vacation rentals tend to book well before the season begins. Read on for 11 of the best Airbnbs for skiing in Europe, from the Austrian, Italian, Swiss, and German Alps to the quaint ski villages of Norway and Slovenia—all according to a skier who can't wait to hit the slopes. We've vetted these listings based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, previous guest reviews, and decor. Why we love it: Mountain views, sauna, hammam, movie theater, ski storage, concierge, cleaning service, optional private chefThis group-friendly ski rental is ideal for friends and families alike, with plenty of room to sprawl and amenities to appreciate. You can start each day with a breakfast prepared by the in-house chef and enjoy the meal in the dining room with views of the sprawling snow-capped peaks. Unwind in the sauna or steam room before gathering the crew for a movie in the private cinema room. Don't forget about the à la carte services, too; you can create your own stay from Le Collectionist's full range of services and tailor-made experiences like transfers upon arrival and departure, groceries delivered before arrival, car rentals, private chef and/or ski instructors, as well as a ski fitting at home. As part of the site's spiffy Signature collection, you're also entitled to daily cleaning services, a dedicated concierge, a personalized welcome, and restaurant recommendations and reservations. Nestled in the Austrian Alps, guests of this chalet will find themselves in the heart of picture-perfect St. Anton, widely known as the “cradle of alpine skiing.” And while skiing here goes way back to the early 20th century, you'll find there's much to fall in love with today, too—from state-of-the-art lifts to a buzzy yet less-crowded après-ski scene. City: St. Anton, Austria Things to do nearby: Museum St. Anton am Arlberg, Schwarzwassersee, Ski Arlberg (St. Anton, St. Christoph, Stuben), HarborWalk Village Why we love it: Heated swimming pool, hot tub, gym, ski storage, mountain and village views, sauna, fireplaceThis iconic ski village, Verbier, is known for its legendary freeride lines, vibrant après-ski scene, and sun-drenched panoramas of the Alps. Arguably, it has the most lift-accessible off-piste skiing in the region, yet it still offers a vast amount of piste skiing for beginners and intermediates. Those who stay at this villa will be within walking distance to it all. This is another Signature property from Le Collectionist—so you can take advantage of all the perks and à la carte services available. item.title: Backpacker Rescued in Central Arizona After Floods Sweep Away His Gear
item.description:
Source: Backpacker Magazine
Search and rescue teams mobilized to help a backpacker in Arizona’s Yavapai County on October 24 after a swollen creek swept his camping gear away. Fall in Yavapai County typically comes with cool, dry conditions, making it a popular time for hikers to log time on the trail. But the National Weather Service issued a flood watch for northern and central Arizona on October 21 that remained in effect through the evening of the 22, advising visitors to be wary of flash flooding potential in areas that are normally dry or low. A strong storm brought damaging winds, large hail, and flash floods across the region from a system that came from the California coast. The man was seven days into his backpacking trip when he lost his equipment. He managed to send a message to family alerting them about his situation just before his phone’s battery died. Rescuers with the Yavapai County Sheriff’s Office (YCSO) Aviation Team, Forest Patrol, and SAR volunteers responded to the incident, combing the area near Sheep Bridge off Bloody Basin Road for any clues to the hiker’s whereabouts. On Saturday morning, aerial crews spotted the hiker, and brought him to safety. “Although he was exhausted, scratched up, and at his physical limits, he was in good health,” the YCSO wrote. This incident came just one day after the Yavapai County Sheriff’s Office received a call about a group of four people who were sitting on the top of a car while floods swept through the Wet Beaver Creek crossing near Dragonshead and Culpepper Ranch roads. Deputies said that the vehicle moved about 150 feet downstream. Footage from the rescue shows swift muddied water at about the height of the vehicle’s headlights. While rain in October is normal in central Arizona, extensive flooding is less common. Rainfall reports showed that parts of Yavapai County received more than an inch of precipitation over the course of 48 hours, putting them at a much higher risk of flash flooding. In response to the first incident, Yavapai County Sheriff’s officials urged hikers to, “know your physical limitations, understand trail conditions, and check the weather forecast for your route.”

item.title: REVIEW: This Under-$30 Eye Mask Helps Me Sleep on Red-Eyes
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler
Despite taking countless red-eye flights over the past 20 years, I've never been able to crack the code on how to sleep on a plane. If I’m being totally honest, I’m pretty lousy at it: A bout of rough air will jolt me awake in a sheer panic, and fellow passengers' screens and the plane's overhead lights will keep me up for hours. By the time I’ve reached my destination, I’m usually exhausted and cranky, and rocking a killer headache. Truthfully, I was tired of being tired after a flight. All of my jet-setting friends swear by wearing an eye mask on the plane, but finding one I actually liked proved to be a challenge. The cheap ones handed out by flight attendants are…well, cheap—and they're usually too tight around my head. Other sleep masks I've tried in the past would press down on my eyelids, which was incredibly uncomfortable (and felt like a stye waiting to happen). My luck changed when I stumbled upon Zimasilk's sleep mask on Amazon a few months ago, and it’s been smooth, surprisingly sleep-filled flying ever since. The eye mask’s buttery-soft, 100% mulberry silk fabric is what initially drew me in. According to the brand, it's completely covered in 22 Momme Grade 6A silk, which is pretty high-end for the mask’s under-$30 price point. Mulberry silk is naturally smooth and temperature-regulating, and is gentle on the skin. It feels so nice—a small touch of luxury that makes me like I'm sitting in first class. The mask comes in 11 different colorways, from beige and black to plum and sky blue, all with a sleek sheen. The soft material might’ve piqued my interest, but the 3D-molded eye cups are what sold me. The chambers completely block out light, and they're roomy enough that I can comfortably blink while wearing it (which is more than I can say for most eye masks on the market). Plus, it's not bulky at all—the lightweight, packable design of the mask makes it an ideal choice for travelers. I simply fold it up and slip it into a pocket or side compartment of my carry-on. Once I’m settled in my seat, I can tinker with the adjustable band to get a Goldilocks fit—snug, but not too tight—and be ready for takeoff in no time. I’m not the only one who’s a fan of Zimasilk's sleep mask. For a while, my husband was convinced he didn’t need to spend $27 on an eye mask. But ever since he tried mine, he's totally converted, and even got one for himself that he's been wearing everywhere from planes to hotel rooms. As expected, the contoured eye mask doesn’t magically keep me from jolting awake during turbulence, but it does make falling asleep a lot easier. I’ve traveled to six different time zones over the past five weeks—on trips to Fiji, London, Croatia, Greece, Chicago, and San Francisco—and have been able to get at least a little bit of sleep on each flight. Perhaps my best sleep streak was on an 11-hour red-eye to Fiji, where I miraculously spent at least half the time sleeping. When my husband and I finally made it to our hotel in Savusavu, I was surprisingly upbeat. (A red-eye rarity, if you ask me.) And, thanks to this mask, I can fall asleep during daytime itineraries, too: I was recently on a morning flight from Athens to London and conked out for hours. When I finally woke up, I noticed some nearby passengers awkwardly glancing my way. Who knows…maybe I was sleeping so deeply that I was snoring—or maybe they were just jealous I found the secret to an in-flight snooze.

item.title: REVIEW: Review: Salomon X Ultra 5 Mid GTX
item.description:
Source: Sectionhiker.com
The Salomon XT Ultra 5 Mid GTX is a sturdy hiking boot designed for walkers who want dependable protection without the excessive weight and stiffness of traditional leather footwear. With a supportive mid-height collar, a waterproof membrane, and an aggressive outsole, it targets day hikers, fast walkers, and anyone who regularly covers uneven ground in changeable weather. It feels more athletic than a conventional boot, but it still provides the structure needed for rocky trails and loaded daypacks. - Weight: 16.5 oz per shoe (Men’s 10.5) - Mid-height design for added ankle coverage - Waterproof construction for rainy conditions - Lugged outsole for grip on mud, gravel, and loose ground The Salomon X Ultra 5 Mid GTX has a secure, foot-hugging fit that helps keep the heel in place. This is particularly useful on steep descents, where unwanted foot movement can cause discomfort and blisters. The lacing system allows you to adjust the fit across the forefoot and ankle. The padded collar provides comfortable support without feeling excessively stiff. The boot likely suits people with average or slightly narrow feet and average lower calf sizes. Hikers with wide feet or thick ankles should try it on before purchasing, especially if they intend to wear thick hiking socks. Comfort is one of the boot’s main strengths. The cushioning reduces the impact of hard surfaces, while the supportive platform helps keep feet comfortable over longer distances. The X Ultra 5 Mid GTX feels more like an athletic hiking shoe than a traditional heavy boot, making it suitable for walkers who prefer a lighter, more flexible design. The sole and upper feel slightly firm during the first few walks. However, this firmness improves stability on uneven trails and becomes less noticeable as the boots break in after a few miles. The mid-height collar offers more ankle coverage than a low-cut trail shoe while keeping more freedom of movement than a heavy backpacking boot. It offers useful support on uneven ground, though it isn’t intended for highly technical mountain routes or very heavy loads. Its main benefit is proprioception, alerting you to uneven ground; you can still twist an ankle in these mids, or any other mid-height boot, by accident. A reinforced toe area protects against roots, stones, and accidental impacts. I’ve been using these mids during stick season here in Vermont, where fallen leaves obscure the roots and rocks lying in wait underneath. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by the stability these mids offer and the protection the toe kicks provide. I’ll be using these mids for the rest of the autumn hiking season. The durable upper, woven with Kevlar threads for added durability, also gives the boots a reliable feel on woodland paths, rocky trails, and rough countryside routes. The Salomon X Ultra 5 Mid delivers strong traction on a range of common hiking surfaces. Its lugged outsole performs well on: The outsole provides useful braking grip when walking downhill. However, smooth wet rock remains challenging and relies on good footwear. Overall, the traction is dependable for everyday hiking and mixed-terrain walking. The waterproof construction helps keep feet dry in rain, damp grass, and shallow puddles. As long as water doesn’t enter over the collar, the boots offer effective protection on wet-weather hikes. The main compromise is breathability. Waterproof materials can feel warm in hot weather, especially with thick socks. For summer hiking in dry conditions, a non-waterproof trail shoe may feel cooler. For autumn, winter, and rainy spring walks, however, the waterproofing is a valuable feature. - May be narrow for people with wide feet The Salomon X Ultra 5 Mid GTX is a capable waterproof hiking boot with a secure fit, dependable traction, comfortable cushioning, and useful ankle protection. Its lightweight design makes it easier to walk quickly and reduces fatigue compared with heavier boots. Although it can feel warm in summer and may not support heavy backpacking, it performs well in the conditions most day hikers encounter. For walkers looking for a reliable all-weather hiking boot, the Salomon X Ultra 5 Mid is a strong choice. Highly Recommended! .Disclosure: Salomon donated shoes for review. item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to spend five days in Hong Kong: what to eat, see and do across the glittering city
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
The pair of us have spent the past two decades covering what Hong Kong eats and how it lives – and we still can’t agree on who makes the city’s best milk tea. Along the way, we’ve written and edited dozens of guides, ranging from single neighbourhoods to Hong Kong as a whole, and sat on numerous judging panels, all to help visitors get to know this place and fall in love with it the way we have. What follows is a first-timer’s guide to the essentials: the places we take friends who are new to the city, and the ones we make a point of revisiting ourselves because they never stop being fun. Part of what keeps us here is how much Hong Kong fits into a small space. In a single day, you can eat dim sum beside retirees studying the racing pages, ride a tram that’s run along the island since the early 20th century, hike a trail overlooking the South China Sea and end the night with world-class cocktails. Only about a quarter of the territory is built up, with much of the rest protected country park, so beaches and fishing villages are often an easy bus trip from the busiest streets. Public transport makes it easy to reach all of this, and we’ve built each day around it, so you can spend your time exploring rather than retracing your steps. Kick things off with breakfast at Wah Lok, a nostalgic cha chaan teng (a uniquely Hong Kong, East-meets-West diner) that’s been going since the 1940s; grab a booth seat, scrambled egg sandwich and silky-smooth milk tea. Suitably fuelled up, wander down to Hollywood Road for a moment of tranquillity among the gigantic incense coils at Man Mo Temple – one of the city’s oldest Taoist temples. Keep strolling to Cat Street antique market; the various trinkets, ceramics, jade ornaments and vintage-style posters might stretch the definition of “antique”, but it’s ideal for browsing or picking up a souvenir. Caffeine fiends can pause to refuel at Halfway Coffee; their brews being served in vintage Chinese crockery somehow makes the coffee taste even better. Mosey down to Tai Kwun, an arts and culture hub comprising 16 beautifully restored heritage buildings including the former Central Police Station and Victoria Prison, with exhibitions and guided tours that delve deeper into its history. All that exploring works up quite the appetite, so head down the Mid-Level Escalators – the world’s longest outdoor covered escalator – to Mak An Kee, a gloriously old-school wonton joint for your fill of bite-sized prawn dumplings and springy noodles. From there, it’s just a short walk to Central Market, a striking Bauhaus-style building that previously housed one of Hong Kong’s oldest wet markets. Nowadays, you’ll find retro-style souvenir shops, quirky local brands and casual eateries – including freshly-made gai daan zai (egg puff waffles) at Mammy Pancake. Close the day in style with an unforgettable seasonal tasting menu at Mono, where Venezuelan chef-owner Ricardo Chaneton brilliantly fuses Latin American flavours with European technique, before sneaking in a creative cocktail nightcap at acclaimed Japanese bar Gokan. Despite its reputation as a concrete jungle, 40 per cent of Hong Kong comprises protected country parks – so get a dose of the great outdoors by hitting the Morning Trail. Starting at Hatton Road in Central, the incline is steep, but the incredible views as you ascend to The Peak are more than worth it. Reward yourself with a heaven-sent sourdough egg tart from Bakehouse, before soaking up more wow-worthy vistas strolling the Peak Circle Walk. Hop onto the iconic Peak Tram – Asia’s first funicular railway, in operation since 1888 – and admire the dizzying cityscapes as you whizz down to Central. The tram’s Central Terminus helpfully deposits you a short walk from the peaceful greenery of Hong Kong Park. Say hi to the turtles in the lake and admire 60-plus bird species at Edward Youde Aviary, before stopping for a refined lunch of vegetarian dim sum in the traditional teahouse setting of LockCha – where you can choose from over 100 varieties of Chinese tea. Head down to Pacific Place Mall and take the MTR (Mass Transit Railway) to the ever-bustling Causeway Bay, where you can live out all your retail dreams; think luxe designer flagships, Asian beauty meccas, stylish independent boutiques and 17 floors of everything you could ever need at SOGO department store. For dinner, treat yourself to an Indian fine dining feast at Leela, where regional specialities meet Hong Kong-inspired creations for a one-of-a-kind culinary journey. Start the day in Sham Shui Po, a vibrant urban neighbourhood in Kowloon. Grab a plate of the silkiest, freshly made cheong fan (rice noodle rolls) doused in the perfect ratio of sesame, sweet and soy sauce at Hop Yik Tai – they sell 5,000 of them daily. Wind your way to Apliu Street and embrace the chaos of its flea-market stalls overflowing with every vintage electronic imaginable; craft fiends will also love wandering around nearby Ki Lung Street, Nam Cheong Street and Yu Chau Street to admire their aesthetically pleasing rows of colourful buttons, ribbons and beads. Jump back on the MTR to Mong Kok for lunch at the nostalgic London Restaurant, where trolleys piled high with steaming baskets of dim sum weave between the tables. From the chaos to the calm; take a 10-minute taxi to Chi Lin Nunnery and Nan Lian Garden, a peaceful Buddhist temple complex filled with tranquil gardens, lush landscaping, traditional wooden buildings and a spectacular golden pavilion. The contrasting skyscraper surroundings make this serene escape feel even more special. Snag a taxi back to Sham Shui Po for another quintessential Hong Kong experience – eating at a dai pai dong (open-air food stall). Opened in 1956, Oi Man Sang is one of the oldest still standing; watch the chefs cooking up a storm in the street (yes, there will be flames), before feasting on the spoils. Don’t miss the salt-and-pepper squid and black pepper beef and potatoes. Make your way to Tung Chung to ride the Ngong Ping 360 cable car to the Big Buddha; daredevils can opt for a crystal cabin, featuring floor-to-ceiling windows with vertigo-inducing views. Once you’ve arrived, gird your loins for the 268-step hike to the Big Buddha – granting you an up-close look at this majestic 34-metre statue cast from 260 tonnes of bronze. Camera roll filled, it’s time for some island exploring. Take the Lantau Bus 21 to Tai O, Hong Kong’s oldest fishing village, famed for its picturesque stilt houses teetering atop the waterways. Head to the UNESCO-recognised Tai O Heritage Hotel (the former Tai O Police Station) for a relaxing lunch at its glass-roofed restaurant, Tai O Lookout. Bask in ocean vistas while sampling signature dishes crafted with local ingredients like shrimp paste and mountain begonia. Walk off lunch with a leisurely wander around the island, taking in the coastal scenery while snacking on a sugar-dusted sa yong (oversized fluffy Chinese doughnut) from Tai O Bakery. Catch the Lantau Bus 11 back to Tung Chung, then MTR to Jordan in time for some evening fun. Make the most of golden hour with a tipple or two on the leafy rooftop terrace at Terrible Baby. Duly refreshed, head to Temple Street Night Market for sensory overload in the best possible way – think jam-packed souvenir stalls, traditional fortune tellers, live Cantonese opera performances and street food galore. If you fancy something more substantial for dinner, amble over to Hing Kee on Nathan Road for a showstopper serving of typhoon shelter crab – wok-fried whole and loaded with addictively crunchy garlic, black beans, scallions and chillies. Set sail to Tsim Sha Tsui via the Star Ferry, a Hong Kong icon that’s been carrying passengers across the harbour for over 120 years; the journey lasts mere minutes, but the skyline panoramas are pure cinema. Once you disembark, walk along the waterfront for more gorgeous vistas; you’ll also spot the historic former Kowloon-Canton Railway Clock Tower standing tall and a bronze statue of kung fu legend Bruce Lee. Make your way to the ultra-glam Rosewood Hong Kong for lunch – in the form of afternoon tea. Yes, we’re making it a thing. The city’s British colonial past means that afternoon tea is something of an institution here – and the one at Rosewood’s elegant Butterfly Room runs from noon onwards. Indulge in picture-perfect finger sandwiches, buttery scones with all the accoutrements and divinely decadent desserts. Float down from your dessert high to grab a quick taxi to West Kowloon Cultural District, where you’ll find M+ – Asia’s global museum of contemporary art, housed in an impressive Herzog & de Meuron-designed building. Dive into 33 immersive galleries of twentieth- and twenty-first-century works spanning visual art, design and architecture, including an exhibition dedicated to Hong Kong’s retro neon signs. Walk to The Ritz-Carlton, Hong Kong and take your evening to new heights (literally) with sublime sundowners at Ozone – the world’s highest rooftop bar, with sensational views as standard. Jump back onto the MTR to Central and make a beeline to Four Seasons Hotel, Hong Kong, to end your trip with some major culinary fireworks at Lung King Heen, their two-Michelin-starred Chinese restaurant. Enjoy one last dose of those magnificent harbour views while savouring a banquet of exceptional Cantonese cuisine – their succulent char siu barbecue pork is the perfect finale to your Hong Kong experience.

item.title: SALES: Stay Dry, Stay Warm, Stay Out
item.description:
Source: Outside Magazine
No surprise, experience counts in the outdoors. Reading the weather, navigating terrain, choosing the right gear—all those skills improve the more time you spend in the mountains. And that’s why Berghaus, with 60 years of experience crafting outdoor apparel, is revered by adventurers of all stripes. Berghaus was founded in 1966 by Gordon Davison and Peter Lockey, climbing partners who wanted to share their passion for the wilderness and technical expertise with like-minded outdoor lovers. From the brand’s base in Northeast England, it began designing apparel and equipment that offered a pioneering blend of comfort, durability, and protection in harsh environments, and has continued to innovate for six decades. That made Berghaus well-known in the United Kingdom and Europe, and now this storied brand is available in the United States, both online and at retailers across the country. For a great introduction to the Berghaus design heritage and philosophy, check these three standout products. Berghaus was forged in the mountains, where rock-solid protection is mission critical. The Kara-Su 7000 GTX Jacket can handle the elements, whatever the weather brings, thanks to a three-layer Gore-Tex Pro waterproof/breathable membrane. The material, which is revered as Gore’s most protective and durable membrane, boasts a 28,000mm hydrostatic head and will keep you dry no matter how wet things get. The Gore-Tex Pro membrane is only the start of the fortress-like protection. Also key: You can completely batten down the Kara-Su 7000 in the face of intense wind and driving rain. The hem and cuffs are both adjustable—the latter via robust metal snaps—and the jacket’s hood features Berghaus’s trail-tested Mera Peak design, which provides four points of adjustment so you can dial in the fit and coverage without compromising sightlines. Five pockets, including a chest stash pocket and two high hand pockets (placed above a pack hipbelt), ensure must-have items are instantly accessible. Like all Berghaus apparel, the Kara-Su 7000 GTX is as eye-catching as it is functional. Three colorways employ bold styling, and heritage embroidery nods to the brand’s legacy. The best pants adapt to variable conditions so you don’t have to. The Kara-Su Pant is designed to do just that, with a modern, straight-leg fit and articulated knees that promote unrestricted movement. Adjustable ankle cords let you tighten or roll up the cuffs as needed. The pant’s polyamide/elastane material provides a touch of warmth and is also windproof, which goes a long way toward maintaining all-conditions comfort. Smart details also include a button snap and fly closure and belt loops for a precise fit, as well as two hand pockets and a rear pocket. Style bonus: A retro patch on the leg provides a pop of color. A Berghaus hallmark: blending modern outdoor performance with throwback aesthetics. The Kara-Su Sweater is an outstanding example, with its vintage style, vivid colorblocking, and classic embroidered Extrem 7000 logo. The look is bolstered by an oversize cut that makes the Kara-Su super-comfortable and easy to layer under. The sweater’s ribbed cuffs and hem ensure it fits exactly the way you want, and they increase both durability and timeless appeal. The brushed jersey fabric is soft, warm, and feels fantastic on skin. This is a do-it-all layer that feels just as cozy on an all-day hike as it does on a lazy lounging day. Founded in 1966 in Newcastle upon Tyne, UK, Berghaus is a global leader in premium outdoor outerwear, known for innovative designs and lasting durability. From pioneering lightweight rucksacks to iconic Gore-Tex jackets, Berghaus equips adventurers to tackle the elements.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: The ultimate guide to saving money with Amex Offers
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
The ultimate guide to saving money with Amex Offers Getting the most out of every dollar you spend isn't just about redeeming your points and miles for the most value you can. It's also about getting as many rewards as you can from every purchase you make. That often involves looking beyond your credit card's earning categories to promotions, deals and shopping portals. Issuer offers are one way to get more out of your spending. American Express cardmembers can achieve this through Amex Offers. Here's everything you need to know. What are Amex Offers? American Express gives cardmembers the chance to earn additional points or cash back by activating offers within their account. These offers either have a specific spending requirement or allow you to earn additional rewards per dollar spent. They're almost always tied to specific merchants, but some offers may count any spending on your card toward the bonus rewards offered. All Amex Offers require enrollment, so you may miss out on big savings if you don't check your account often. Amex Offers generally vary by card, but there may be some overlap, especially if the cards in question are from the same family. If you see the same offer across multiple cards, know that you can only enroll in it on one of them. Make sure to pick the card that makes the most sense for your spending. For example, my American Express® Gold Card has an offer for 10% back on a single purchase at Cracker Barrel (up to a total of $6 back). While this offer is also available on another Amex card, activating it on my Amex Gold instead will let me take advantage of the Gold's 4 points per dollar spent on dining at restaurants worldwide*. *On up to $50,000 in spending per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar spent. Navigate to your account's home screen and scroll down. You should find a section titled "Amex Offers and Benefits". Here, you can find all of the offers you've enrolled in and the ones still available for enrollment. On the Amex mobile app, navigate to the Offers tab via the navigation bar at the bottom of your screen. Similar to the desktop page, you'll be able to see both your available offers and your enrolled offers. There's no limit to how many Amex Offers you can enroll in at once, aside from the earlier restriction I mentioned regarding enrolling for the same Amex Offer across multiple cards. Keep in mind that all Amex Offers have expiration dates, so make sure to set a reminder for yourself if needed. Once you've enrolled in an offer, you should receive your bonus points or cash back within six to eight weeks after completing the associated spending requirements, but it may take longer depending on the offer. Generally, though, you'll get your bonus rewards a lot faster than that. If you don't see your bonus points or cash back posted after six to eight weeks and you're certain you met the offer requirements, call Amex at the number on the back of your card or contact them via online chat. Note that we've seen datapoints suggesting certain Amex Offers have limited payouts, meaning Amex will only honor a certain number of activated offers. It's advisable to use an offer sooner rather than later when it appears on your account, but this problem isn't too common. Use other shopping portals to maximize rewards You can stack Amex Offers with offers from external shopping portals like Rakuten and Rove. Rakuten is an especially appealing pick if you have an Amex Membership Rewards card, since you can opt to earn Membership Rewards points through Rakuten offers instead of cash back. I enjoy using Rove because of its extensive roster of transfer partners — over 20 at the time of writing — and its range of deals on shopping and travel purchases. Even though I earn Membership Rewards through Rakuten, there are times when I may pair an Amex Offer with a Rove offer instead if the bonus is significantly better. If you have a MaxRewards Gold account, you can link your American Express cards and enjoy auto-activation for all of your Amex Offers. Given that MaxRewards Gold starts at $108 annually, I don't recommend it for just this particular benefit. However, if you can take advantage of the subscription's other perks or you're already a member, this is a great way to avoid forgetting to enroll in an offer before making a purchase. Amex Offers are a great way to stack additional points or cash back on purchases you were already planning to make. Many of American Express's cards have annual fees in the hundreds, so earning extra rewards through Amex Offers is a great way to further justify paying a steep annual fee. Just remember to track the end dates and additional terms on every offer you enroll in. You don't want to miss out by making your purchase after the offer expires. Terms & restrictions apply.
